rows.mechanism: honorWidgetBorderStyle, one new option in the shared finalizer, default off, adjacent to suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders rather than an extension of it. THE ROOT CAUSE, WHICH IS NARROWER AND MORE SPECIFIC THAN THE ASSIGNMENT'S PREMISE AND IS WHAT THE BYTES SAY. /BS /S is a widget's border STYLE (ISO 32000-1 12.5.4, Table 166): it says WHERE the border colour in /MK /BC is painted. /S and the three decorated styles bound the whole rectangle, /N paints nothing, and /U means one thing only -- 'a single line along the bottom of the annotation rectangle'. pdf-lib's default text appearance provider never reads /BS /S and strokes a full rectangle from /MK /BC whatever the style says. On the pinned PA-RCRIM-P-490-ORDER, enumerated here from the binary, EIGHT widgets carry /MK /BC [0 0 0]: six declare NO /BS -- so the default solid style -- and each ships an /AP /N of the form '0 G 0.5 0.5 W H re s', a stroked rectangle, so regenerating one coincides with the form; the other TWO are exactly the two the packet writes into, DocketNumber and Defendant on page 1, both declaring /BS << /S /U >> and both shipping an /AP /N of the form '0 G 0 0.5 m <width> 0.5 l s', one horizontal rule and nothing else. The source is entirely self-consistent; pdf-lib is what disagrees with it. WHY THE OPTION IS NOT A DELETION OF /MK /BC, MEASURED BEFORE THE MECHANISM WAS CHOSEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The pinned order page 1 was rendered twice at 300 dpi, once whole and once with /Annots and /AcroForm removed. In the window of DocketNumber the page content carries 0 dark pixels against 2,680 whole, and at Defendant 0 against 2,856. The court's writing rule at those two blanks exists ONLY inside the widget's own appearance stream. Since regeneration replaces that stream, dropping /MK /BC alone would remove the box AND the rule -- trading a border the form does not print for the loss of a rule the form does. The same measurement explains the control: at DefendantName on the same page, which carries no /BC, the rule IS page content (4,686 pixels with and without annotations), which is why that widget never showed the defect. SO THE OPTION HONOURS THE DECLARED STYLE IN TWO HALVES. Before form.updateFieldAppearances(), /MK /BC is removed from the eligible widget so pdf-lib synthesises no rectangle -- verified in the generated stream, which then ends its path 'h h' with no stroke operator instead of 'h S'. After it, and before any placement, the underline the style declares is drawn back into the regenerated appearance in its own /BBox space from that same /MK /BC and the widget's /BS /W: 'q <colour> RG <W> w [] 0 d 0 <W/2> m <bbox width> <W/2> l S Q'. What that reconstructs is the source's own stream: /BS /W defaults to 1 under 12.5.4, the stroke is centred at W/2, and the two Pennsylvania widgets ship exactly '0 G 0 0.5 m <bbox width> 0.5 l s'. TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS MUST AGREE BEFORE A WIDGET IS TOUCHED, which is also why this satisfies the assignment's own framing. The widget must DECLARE an underline in /BS /S, and its shipped /AP /N must paint no box -- decided by counting the segments of each painted subpath rather than by a substring, because a box is 're' or a painted subpath of three or more segments while a rule is one, and because 's' (closepath-stroke) on a two-point line is a rule and not a box. Where the two signals contradict each other the widget is refused and counted, never repaired, and an /AP that cannot be read is refused on the same terms. WHY NOT suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders. Its contract, in its own words in three places, is that it acts only on 'a field this run did NOT write' and that 'a written value must keep whatever the pipeline draws for it'. Widening it would have broken that documented promise and would have moved the bytes of co_multiple_conviction_seal-set, the one family already opted into it. The new option never reaches an unwritten field and the old one never reaches a written one, so the two cannot overlap; control 13 of the test measures exactly that. Scope: only a TEXT field, only a field this run wrote, only a widget declaring /S /U whose own appearance agrees, and only under the opt-in -- so every caller that does not pass it is byte-unaffected.

scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-active-: contentStreamOperators: a small content-stream tokenizer that skips strings, hex strings, names, numbers and comments, so 're' inside /Frame or inside '(a re b)' is never read as the rectangle operator.

sourceAppearancePaintsRectangle (exported): does the appearance the SOURCE ships paint a box? Decided by counting the segments of each painted subpath -- 're', or a painted subpath of three or more segments, is a box; one segment is a rule. Returns null for no /AP, a state dictionary, or an undecodable stream, and every caller treats null as 'paints a box'.

declaredUnderlineBorder (exported): the underline a widget DECLARES, from /BS /S, /BS /W and /MK /BC only. A /BS /W of 0 paints no border under 12.5.4 and a /BC that sets no colour paints none under 12.5.6.19; both return null. Handles 1, 3 and 4 component colours as G, RG and K.

takeDeclaredUnderlineBordersOffWidgets (exported): before appearances are generated, removes /MK /BC from every widget of a WRITTEN text field that declares an underline and ships an appearance agreeing there is no box, and returns what must be drawn back. Refusals are counted in two named buckets.

drawDeclaredUnderlineBorders (exported): after appearances are generated and before any placement, draws the declared underline into each regenerated appearance in its own /BBox space, last so no text clip can remove it, inside its own q/Q so the graphics state is left as found.
